raw_case_text:
A previously healthy 67-year-old man presented with an acute onset of back pain, followed by progressive numbness and weakness of the limbs for 1 week. He could still ambulate with minimal help. On the day he was admitted to our hospital, his condition aggravated suddenly and reached a plateau within 8 h. He developed urinary retention and could barely raise his arms or move his legs. His family members mentioned that he also became irritable and forgetful. The neurological examination revealed severe quadriparesis (Medical Research Council strength score, upper extremities: grade 3; lower extremities: grade 1), a sensory C4 level, tendon hyperreflexia, and Hoffmann and Babinski sign. Physical examination was unremarkable.
Laboratory investigations including full blood counts, thyroid function, liver and renal function, LDH, beta2-microglobulin, and tumor markers were normal. HIV antibodies and syphilis antibodies were negative. Antibodies mediating autoimmune encephalitis (anti-NMDAR, -AMPAR, -LG1, -CASPR2, -GABABR) or paraneoplastic syndromes (anti-Yo, -Hu, -Ri, -CV2, -amphiphysin, -PNMA2) in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and serum were negative, so were antibodies against aquaporin-4 (AQP-4), myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG), and myelin basic protein (MBP). CSF analysis revealed normal CSF pressure, a mild pleocytosis (8 cells/ml) without atypical or malignant cells, an elevated protein level (132.9 mg/dl), and normal glucose and chlorine levels. Bacterial and fungal cultures were negative. CSF IgG index was 0.17, and the IgG oligoclonal bands were absent. Brain MRI revealed multifocal periventricular lesions with gadolinium enhancement in the left medial temporal lobe (Figures 1A-C). Spine MRI revealed longitudinally extensive abnormal signal extending from the cervical to the thoracic cord (Figure 1D).
The patient was suspected to have inflammatory demyelinating disease with a working diagnosis of ADEM or serologically negative NMOSD. He was treated with intravenous methylprednisolone (1 g/d for 5 days), followed by prednisone taper, and his condition markedly improved. The back pain was substantially relieved. Neurological examination revealed improved extremity strength (upper extremities: grade 4+; lower extremities: grade 4), with a sensory level of T12. He was subsequently treated with intravenous immunoglobulin, but without further improvement. The patient was discharged to rehabilitation.
For the following 6 months, the patient's condition remained stable. He could ambulate with minimal help. However, the 6-month follow-up brain MRI revealed an unexpected enhancing temporal mass with extensive perifocal edema (Figures 1F-H). Repeat spine MRI revealed decreasing lesions without contrast enhancement (Figure 1E). Brain stereotactic biopsy of the right temporal mass was performed. Histopathological findings of the specimen demonstrated DLBCL (Figure 2). Whole-body positron-emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) imaging was performed to evaluate extra-neural involvement. Abnormal hypermetabolism was found in the left testicle and in multiple abdominal and retroperitoneal lymph nodes (Figure 3). Subsequent testicle and bone marrow biopsies were consistent with DLBCL (Stage IV disease).
Systemic chemotherapy (Methotrexate + Rituximab + Ara-C) combined with involved field radiotherapy was conducted. Due to severe vomiting, the chemotherapy had to be discontinued after the fourth therapy cycle. Repeat brain MRI showed necrosis of the original mass lesion, no new lesions were observed (Figures 1I,J). Sixteen months after the initial admission, he could ambulate by himself without any help.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 67-year-old previously healthy man presented with a 1-week history of acute back pain and progressive four-limb numbness and weakness that abruptly worsened over 8 hours to severe quadriparesis and urinary retention, accompanied by irritability and forgetfulness.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: One week prior to admission, the patient developed acute back pain followed by progressive numbness and weakness in his extremities. On the day of admission, his neurological deficits rapidly worsened within 8 hours to severe quadriparesis and acute urinary retention, while his family noted recent irritability and memory loss. Six months after initial steroid-responsive improvement, follow-up brain MRI detected a new enhancing right temporal lobe mass.
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously healthy with no chronic medical conditions.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for acute back pain, quadriparesis, C4 sensory level, urinary retention, irritability, and forgetfulness.

objective.physical_examination: Neurological examination on admission revealed severe quadriparesis (MRC grade 3/5 in upper extremities, grade 1/5 in lower extremities), a C4 sensory level, diffuse hyperreflexia, bilateral positive Hoffmann and Babinski signs, and urinary retention. General systemic physical examination was unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: CBC, thyroid panel, liver and renal function, LDH, beta2-microglobulin, serum tumor markers, HIV antibodies, and syphilis antibodies were all normal or negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Serum and CSF autoimmune encephalitis panels (NMDAR, AMPAR, LGI1, CASPR2, GABABR), paraneoplastic panels (Yo, Hu, Ri, CV2, amphiphysin, PNMA2), and demyelinating antibodies (AQP4, MOG, MBP) were all negative. Lumbar puncture showed normal opening pressure, mild pleocytosis (8 cells/mL) without malignant cells, elevated protein (132.9 mg/dL), normal glucose/chloride, IgG index 0.17, negative oligoclonal bands, and negative cultures. Initial brain MRI showed multifocal periventricular lesions with left medial temporal gadolinium enhancement, and spine MRI showed a longitudinally extensive cervical-to-thoracic cord lesion. At 6 months, repeat brain MRI revealed a large enhancing right temporal mass with perifocal edema, whole-body FDG PET/CT showed hypermetabolic left testicular and retroperitoneal/abdominal nodal lesions, and stereotactic brain, testicular, and bone marrow biopsies confirmed stage IV diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed stage IV primary testicular diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) with secondary CNS/spinal cord involvement initially mimicking acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) / seronegative NMOSD as a sentinel demyelinating/lymphomatous lesion (syphilis and autoimmune/paraneoplastic encephalomyelitis excluded). Initial high-dose IV methylprednisolone (1 g/day x 5 days) and oral prednisone taper transiently improved limb strength to 4+/5 and 4/5; following 6-month biopsy confirmation of stage IV DLBCL, he received 4 cycles of systemic chemotherapy (high-dose methotrexate, rituximab, and cytarabine) plus involved-field radiotherapy, achieving tumor necrosis on MRI and independent ambulation at 16 months.
